title: Native North American Art
description: A survey of the arts of Native North America, from ancestral processes to contemporary trends. During the first half of the course, we will move across regions to explore different ancestral traditions from basket weaving practices of the Chumash people here in Santa Barbara to wampum belt making of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy in the Northeast. In the remaining weeks, we will shift to pan-Indigenous art debates from the 20th century until today. Students will engage with concepts such as settler colonialism, stereotypes, visual sovereignty, environmental justice, material culture, institutional critique, and the politics of representation.

title: Special Topics in Art of the Americas
description: Special topics in art in the Americas

title: Art of Colonial Mexico
description: This advanced survey explores the art of colonial Mexico, or New Spain, from the 16th through 18th centuries and focuses on art and architectures role in forming a colonial society. We discuss Indigenous experiences of colonialism and forms of resistance as well as how manuscripts, architecture, paintings, maps, featherworks, and public festivals constructed ideas of place, colonial society, and social identity.

title: Mexican Manuscripts
description: This upper division lecture surveys the manuscript traditions of 15th and 16th century Mexico, including Nahua, Mixtec, and Maya codices. Through this course, we explore the importance of books and writing in Mesoamerican cultures; the place of histories, maps, and divinatory almanacs in Mesoamerican thought and society; and the role of Indigenous and European book traditions in shaping the colonial encounter.

title: African Art I
description: The relationship of art to life in sub-Saharan Africa. A cross-cultural survey of types, styles, history, and values of arts ranging from personal decoration to the state festival, stressing Ashanti, Ife, Benin, Yoruba, Cameroon.

title: African Art II
description: An in-depth continuation of Art History 127A in a seminar/discussion format. Selected topics in masking, figural sculpture, etc., and emphasis on African contexts of ritual and social life.

title: Special Topics in African Art
description: Topics cover art and new media and the changing roles of technology, patrons, collectors, museums and other emergent institutions of patronage in contemporary art.

title: Pre-Columbian Art of Mexico
description: The art and architecture of selected cultures of Northern Mesoamerica (non-Maya) from circa 1200 B.C. to the Conquest with an emphasis on iconographical and historical problems.

title: Pre-Columbian Art of the Maya
description: Exploration of the art of Maya-speaking cultures in Southern Mesoamerica using archaeological, epigraphic and ethnographic data to help reconstruct Maya religion and civilization.

title: The Arts of Spain and New Spain
description: Beginning with the Islamic Medieval and Renaissance arts of Spain, this course will chart their influence and transformation in the sixteenth and seventeenth century arts of the new world. Special emphasis on the creativeinteraction of the European and indigenous traditions in colonial arts of the Americans.

title: Art and Archaeology of the Ancient Andes
description: The architecture, ceramics, textiles, and other classes of material culture of Andean societies from 3000 B.C. to the Conquest examined within their cultural contexts with a focus on sociopolitical organization and cultural traditions.

title: Art and Archaeology of Mesoamerica
description: An introduction to the societies of Ancient Mesoamerica. The course examines sociopolitical, religious, and economic systems from the Olmec through Aztecs via the study of material culture including art, architecture, and artifacts. Explores topics of identity, social status, and exchange.

title: Art and Architecture of the North Coast of Peru
description: The rise and fall of ancient societies of the north coast of Peru such as the Moche, Sicán, and Chimú as well as their cultural antecedents as understood through the material record including architecture, ceramics, textiles, etc.

title: Special Topics in Latin American Art
description: Special topics in Latin American art.

title: Art of Colonial Mexico
description: Examines the art of colonial Mexico in its major spaces of production: missions, metropolitan churches, colonial cities, indigenous communities, and arenas of global exchange. Discusses a range of art media, including architecture, painting, public festivals, manuscripts, featherworks, and talavera. Also considers how art production in these varied spaces came to form an idea of colonial Mexican art.

title: Mexican Manuscripts
description: This upper division lecture surveys the manuscript traditions of 15th and 16th century Mexico, including Nahua, Mixtec, and Maya codices. Through this course, we explore the importance of books and writing in Mesoamerican cultures; the place of histories, maps, and divinatory almanacs in Mesoamerican thought and society; and the role of Indigenous and European book traditions in shaping the colonial encounter.

title: Mediterranean Cities
description: An exploration of the most important Medieval cities of the Mediterranean world, their urban forms, layout, architecture, and physical patterns. Venice, Cairo, and Baghdad will be among the cities discussed.

title: The Masterpiece in Islamic Art and Architecture
description: Specific objects and buildings as a means towards exploring their types, media, and contextual problems. Objects include works on paper, ceramics, and metalware.

title: Architecture and Ideology from Constantine to Suleyman the Magnificent
description: Byzantine and Islamic architecture.

title: Islamic Architecture 650-1400
description: Islamic architecture between 650 and 1400 in its historical context.

title: Islamic Architecture 1400-Modern
description: Islamic architecture, 1400-modern, in its historical context.

title: Monuments of Power
description: Historical documents and contemporary interpretations are used to explore the ways in which messages of dominance and power were embedded into Islamic monuments from the seventh century to modern times. A comparative, cross-cultural approach focusing on the power of architectural monuments in relation to the power to create architectural monuments.

title: Art of Empire
description: Studies the visual culture of different empires, alone or in a comparative fashion. For example, Ottoman and Hapsburg; Ottomoman, Safavid, and Mughal; Mughal and British India; or the earlier empire of the Fatimids, Abbasids, and Umayyads of Syria and Spain.

title: Modern Art of the Arab World
description: Explores modern and contemporary art, artists and art movements of the Arab world from nineteenth century to the present.

title: The Mosque in History
description: Major historical and contemporary issues related to mosques as architecture and as social institutions. Working vocabulary of forms and visual knowledge of major monuments. Global context.

title: Special Topics in Islamic Art
description: Special topics in Islamic art.

title: Buddhist Art
description: A survey of select forms of Indian, Chinese, and Japanese Buddhist art. Emphasis on Buddhist sculpture and Zen painting. Exploration of the correlation of religious values and art, transformation and adaptation of artistic traditions from one culture to another.

title: Early Chinese Art
description: A survey of the art and archaeology of Ancient China, from neolithic times through the Tang Dynasty (A.D. 618-906). Emphasis on the development and transformation of pictorial traditions, leading to early painting theory and practice.

title: Chinese Painting I
description: Chinese painting and theory, from beginnings through the fourteenth century. Introduction to major developments and masters in their cultural context with a focus on meaning and agency.
